Read it aloud, then record yourself: the main stress falls on the content word, not on the hedge.

elements.content: Grammar focus: Reported Speech: Statements.

Move every tense back one step, move the pronouns to the reporter's point of view, and move the time words with them. Keep the tense if the statement is still true and the reporting verb is in the present: she says she is busy.

present → past — tense shift: I am busy → he said he was busy
present perfect → past perfect — earlier action: I have finished → she had finished
will → would — future to conditional: I will call → he would call
can → could, must → had to — modal shift: I can't come → he couldn't come
say vs tell — tell takes a person: he said that / he told me that
time and place words — shift too: now → then, here → there, tomorrow → the next day
Guided practice: choose the correct option.
1. Complete: 'She said she ___ finished.'
2. Complete: 'He ___ me he would call.'
3. Complete: 'They said they ___ attend.'
Read and listen: three examples in context.

I am busy → He said he was busy. — Present to past. (Am becomes was.)
I have finished → She said she had finished. — Perfect to past perfect. (Have becomes had.)
I will call → He said he would call. — Will becomes would. (Future to conditional.)
What do you observe?

Reported statements shift the tense one step back: present simple to past simple, present continuous to past continuous, present perfect to past perfect, will to would, can to could, must to had to. Pronouns and time words shift too: now becomes then, today becomes that day, tomorrow becomes the next day. Say takes no object, tell takes a person: he said that, he told me that.
1. Which verb takes a person as its object?
2. What does will become in reported speech?
State the rule in one sentence, without looking at the table.
Freer production: I can report and analyse advertising messages.

Success criteria:
- I can shift the tense one step back.
- I can choose between say and tell.
- I can change pronouns and time words with the tense.
Role play: put your position in ninety seconds; your partner notes every use of the target structure.
Frequent errors and correction:

❌ He said me that he was busy (say with a person object) → ✅ He told me that he was busy
❌ She said she will send it (future not shifted) → ✅ She said she would send it
Correct these sentences: say what is wrong, then give the right version.
Acceptable variants:

I am reviewing the file → She said she was reviewing the file.
We have signed → They said they had signed.
I must leave → He said he had to leave.
Adapt the same task to the group:

- Individual: five sentences with the structure, on the topic of the lesson.
- Pair: a ten-line dialogue where reported speech: statements carries the argument.
- Group: a six-minute debate, two sides, the structure required in every turn.
- Professional audience: transpose the structure into a memo.
- Academic audience: transpose it into a paragraph of analysis.
